{{Short description|Solution of Einstein field equations}}
{{General relativity sidebar |solutions}}

The '''Kerr–Newman–de–Sitter metric''' (KNdS)<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Stuchlik|last2=Bao|last3=Østgaard |last4=Hledik|title=Kerr-Newman-de Sitter black holes with a restricted repulsive barrier of equatorial photon motion|journal=Physical Review D|date=2008 |volume=58 |page=084003|doi=10.1088/0264-9381/17/21/312|arxiv=0803.2539 |s2cid=250888923 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last1=Griffiths|last2=Podolsky|title=Exact spacetimes in Einstein's General Relativity|publisher=Cambridge University Press |series=Cambridge Monographs in Mathematical Physics|date=2009 |doi=10.1017/CBO9780511635397|isbn=978-0-521-88927-8 }}</ref> is one of the most general [[stationary spacetime|stationary solutions]] of the [[Einstein's field equation#Einstein–Maxwell equations|Einstein–Maxwell equations]] in [[general relativity]] that describes the spacetime geometry in the region surrounding an electrically charged, rotating mass embedded in an expanding universe. It generalizes the [[Kerr–Newman metric]] by taking into account the [[cosmological constant]] <math>\Lambda</math>.

== Boyer–Lindquist coordinates ==
{{Main|Boyer–Lindquist coordinates}}
In those coordinates the local clocks and rulers are at constant <math>\rm r</math> and have no local orbital angular momentum <math>\rm (L_z=0)</math>, therefore they are corotating with the [[frame-dragging]] velocity relative to the fixed stars. In {{nowrap|(+, −, −, −)}} [[Metric signature|signature]] and in [[Nondimensionalization|natural units]] of <math>\rm G=M=c=k_e=1</math> the KNdS metric is<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Garnier|first1=Arthur|title=Motion equations in a Kerr-Newman-de Sitter spacetime|journal=Classical and Quantum Gravity|date=2023 |volume=40 |issue=13 |doi=10.1088/1361-6382/accbfe|arxiv=2307.04073|s2cid=258085066 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Kraniotis|title=Gravitational lensing and frame-dragging of light in the Kerr–Newman and the Kerr–Newman (anti) de Sitter black hole spacetimes|journal=General Relativity and Gravitation|date=2014 |volume=46 |issue=11 |page=1818 |doi=10.1007/s10714-014-1818-8|arxiv=1401.7118 |bibcode=2014GReGr..46.1818K |s2cid=125791608 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Bhattacharya|title=Kerr-de Sitter spacetime, Penrose process and the generalized area theorem|journal=Physical Review D|date=2018 |volume=97 |issue=8 |article-number=084049 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.97.084049|arxiv=1710.00997 |bibcode=2018PhRvD..97h4049B |s2cid=119187422 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Stuchlik|last2=Bao|last3=Østgaard|title=Null Hypersurfaces in Kerr-Newman-AdS Black Hole and Super-Entropic Black Hole Spacetimes|journal=Classical and Quantum Gravity|date=2021 |volume=38 |issue=4 |page=045018 |doi=10.1088/1361-6382/abd3e0|arxiv=2007.04354 |bibcode=2021CQGra..38d5018I |s2cid=220424477 }}</ref>

<math>g_{\rm tt}= \rm -\frac{3 \ [ a^2 \ \sin^2 \theta  \left(a^2 \ \Lambda  \ \cos^2 \theta +3\right)+a^2 \left(\Lambda \ r^2-3\right)+\Lambda \ r^4-3 \ r^2+6 \ r-3 \mho^2 ] }{\left(a^2 \ \Lambda +3\right)^2 \left(a^2 \cos^2 \theta +r^2\right)}</math>

<math>g_{\rm rr}= \rm -\frac{a^2 \ \cos^2 \theta +r^2}{\left(a^2+r^2\right) \left(1-\frac{\Lambda \  r^2}{3}\right)-2 \   r+\mho^2}</math>

<math>g_{\rm \theta \theta}= \rm -\frac{3 \left(a^2 \  \cos^2 \theta +r^2\right)}{a^2 \ \Lambda  \ \cos^2 \theta +3}</math>

<math>g_{\rm \phi \phi}= \rm\frac{9 \ \{  \frac{1}{3} \left(a^2+r^2\right)^2 \sin^2 \theta   \left(a^2 \ \Lambda  \cos^2 \theta +3\right)-a^2 \sin^4 \theta  \  [ \left(a^2+r^2\right) \left(1-\Lambda \  r^2/3\right)-2  \ r+\mho ^2 ] \} }{-\left(a^2 \ \Lambda +3\right)^2 \left(a^2 \cos^2 \theta +r^2\right)}</math>

<math>g_{\rm t \phi}= \rm \frac{3 \ a \ \sin^2 \theta \ [ a^2 \ \Lambda  \left(a^2+r^2\right) \cos^2 \theta +a^2 \ \Lambda \  r^2+\Lambda \  r^4+6 \ r-3 \ \mho^2 ] }{\left(a^2 \ \Lambda +3\right)^2 \left(a^2 \ \cos^2 \theta +r^2\right)}</math>

with all the other metric tensor components <math>g_{\mu \nu}=0</math>, where <math>\rm a</math> is the black hole's spin parameter, <math>\rm \mho</math> its electric charge, and <math>\rm \Lambda=3 H^2 </math><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Gaur|last2=Visser|title=Black holes embedded in FLRW cosmologies|journal=Physical Review D |date=2023 |volume=110 |issue=4 |article-number=043529 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.110.043529 |arxiv=2308.07374|bibcode=2024PhRvD.110d3529G }}</ref> the cosmological constant with <math>\rm H</math> as the time-independent [[De Sitter universe#Mathematical expression|Hubble parameter]]. The [[Electromagnetic potential|electromagnetic 4-potential]] is

<math>\rm A_{\mu } = \left\{\frac{3 \ r \ \mho }{\left(a^2 \ \Lambda +3\right) \left(a^2 \ \cos^2 \theta +r^2\right)}, \ 0, \ 0, \ -\frac{3 \ a \ r \ \mho  \ \sin ^2 \theta }{\left(a^2 \ \Lambda +3\right) \left(a^2 \ \cos^2 \theta +r^2\right)}\right\}</math>

The frame-dragging angular velocity is

<math>\omega  = \frac{\rm d\phi}{\rm d t}= -\frac{g_{\rm t \phi}}{g_{\rm \phi \phi}}= \rm \frac{a \ [ a^2 \ \Lambda  \left(a^2+r^2\right) \cos^2 \theta +a^2 \ \Lambda \  r^2+6  \ r+\Lambda \  r^4-3 \ \mho^2 ] }{a^2 \ \sin^2 \theta \ [ a^2 \left(\Lambda \  r^2-3\right)+6  \ r+\Lambda \  r^4-3 \ r^2-3 \ \mho^2 ] +a^2 \ \Lambda \ \left(a^2+r^2\right)^2 \cos^2 \theta +3 \ \left(a^2+r^2\right)^2}</math>

and the local frame-dragging velocity relative to constant <math>\rm \{r, \theta, \phi \}</math> positions (the speed of light at the [[ergosphere]])

<math>\nu = \sqrt{g_{\rm t \phi} \ g^{\rm t \phi}} = \rm \sqrt{-\frac{a^2 \ \sin^2 \theta   
 \ [ a^2 \ \Lambda  \left(a^2+r^2\right) \cos^2 \theta +a^2 \Lambda \  r^2+6  \ r+\Lambda \  r^4-3 \ \mho^2 ] ^2}{\left(a^2 \ \Lambda  \ \cos^2 \theta +3\right) \left(a^2+r^2-a^2 \sin^2 \theta \right)^2 [ a^2  \left(\Lambda \ r^2-3\right)+6  \ r+\Lambda \ r^4-3 \ r^2-3 \ \mho^2 ] }}</math>

The escape velocity (the speed of light at the horizons) relative to the local corotating zero-angular momentum observer is

<math> {\rm v} = \sqrt{ 1 - 1/g^{\rm tt} } =  \rm \sqrt{\frac{3 \left(a^2 \Lambda  \cos^2 \theta +3\right) \left(a^2+r^2-a^2 \sin^2 \theta \right)^2 \left[a^2 \left(\Lambda  r^2-3\right)+\Lambda  r^4-3 r^2+6 r-3 \mho ^2\right]}{\left(a^2 \Lambda +3\right)^2 \left( a^2 \cos^2 \theta +r^2\right) \{ a^2 \Lambda \left( a^2+r^2 \right)^2 \cos^2 \theta +3 \left( a^2+r^2 \right)^2+a^2 \sin^2 \theta  \left[a^2 \left(\Lambda  r^2-3\right)+\Lambda  r^4-3 r^2+6 r-3 \mho ^2 \right] \} }+1} </math> 

The conserved quantities in the equations of motion

<math>{\rm \ddot{x}^{\mu} = -\sum_{\alpha, \beta}  \ ( \Gamma^{\mu}_{\alpha \beta} \ \dot{x}^{\alpha} \ \dot{x}^{\beta} + q \ { \rm F}^{\mu \beta} \ {\rm \dot{x}}^{\alpha}} \ g_{\alpha \beta})
</math>

where <math>\rm \dot{x}</math> is the [[four velocity]], <math>\rm q</math> is the test particle's [[specific charge]] and <math>\rm F</math> the [[Electromagnetic tensor|Maxwell–Faraday tensor]]

<math>\rm { \ F}_{\mu \nu}=\frac{\partial A_{\mu}}{\partial x^{\nu}}-\frac{\partial A_{\nu}}{\partial x^{\mu}}</math>

are the total energy

<math>{\rm E = -p_t}=g_{\rm tt} {\rm \dot{t}}+g_{\rm t \phi} {\rm \dot{\phi}} + \rm q \ A_{t}</math>

and the covariant axial [[Relativistic angular momentum|angular momentum]]

<math>{\rm L_z = p_{\phi}}=-g_{\rm \phi \phi} {\rm \dot{\phi}}-g_{\rm t \phi} {\rm \dot{t}} - \rm q \ A_{\phi}</math>

The [[Notation for differentiation|overdot]] stands for differentiation by the testparticle's [[proper time]] <math>\tau</math> or the photon's [[affine parameter]], so <math>\rm \dot{x}=dx/d\tau , \ \ddot{x}=d^2x/d\tau^2</math>.

== Null coordinates ==

To get <math>g_{\rm rr}=0</math> coordinates we apply the transformation

<math>\rm dt=du-\frac{dr \left(a^2 \ \Lambda / 3 +1\right) \left(a^2+r^2\right)}{\left(a^2+r^2\right) \left(1-\Lambda \ r^2 / 3 \right)-2 \ r+\mho ^2}</math>

<math>\rm d \phi = d \varphi-\frac{a \ dr \left(a^2 \ \Lambda / 3 +1\right)}{\left(a^2+r^2\right) \left(1-\Lambda \ r^2 / 3 \right)-2  \ r+ \mho ^2} </math>

and get the metric coefficients

<math>g_{\rm ur}=\rm -\frac{3}{a^2 \ \Lambda +3}</math>

<math>g_{\rm r\varphi}=\rm \frac{3 \ a \sin^2 \theta }{a^2 \ \Lambda +3}</math>

<math>g_{\rm uu}=g_{\rm tt} \ , \ \ g_{\theta \theta}=g_{\theta \theta} \ , \ \ g_{\rm \varphi \varphi}=g_{\rm \phi \phi} \ , \ \ g_{\rm u \varphi}=g_{\rm t \phi}</math>

and all the other <math>g_{\mu \nu}=0</math>, with the electromagnetic [[vector potential]]

<math>\rm A_{\mu}=\left\{\frac{3 \ r \ \mho }{\left(a^2 \ \Lambda +3\right) \left(a^2 \cos^2 \theta +r^2\right)},\frac{3 \ r \ \mho }{a^2  \left(\Lambda  \ r^2-3\right)+6  \ r+\Lambda \  r^4-3  \left(r^2+\mho ^2\right)}, \ 0, \ -\frac{3 \ a \ r \ \mho  \sin ^2 \theta }{\left(a^2 \ \Lambda +3\right) \left(a^2 \cos^2 \theta +r^2\right)}\right\}</math>

Defining <math>\rm \bar{t}=u-r</math> ingoing lightlike worldlines give a <math>45^{\circ}</math> light cone on a <math>\{ \rm \bar{t}, \ r \}</math> [[spacetime diagram]].

== Horizons and ergospheres ==

[[File:Kerr_Newman_De_Sitter_(KNdS)_Horizons_&_Ergospheres.gif|thumb|right|280px|Horizons and ergosheres in the KNdS metric for different M:Λ ratios. The black hole related surfaces are color coded as in [[:File:Kerr-surfaces.png|here]].]]
[[File:Kerr Newman De Sitter (KNdS) Horizons vs Ergospheres.png|thumb|right|280px|Left: horizons, right: ergosheres for M=1, a=9/10, ℧=2/5, Λ=1/9. At this point the black hole's outer ergosphere has joined the cosmic one to form two domes around the black hole.]]
[[File:Orbit in the Kerr Newman De Sitter Spacetime.png|thumb|right|280px|Unstable orbit at r=2 with the black hole and cosmic parameters as in the image above.]]
The horizons are at <math>g^{\rm rr}=0</math> and the ergospheres at <math>g_{\rm tt}||g_{\rm uu}=0</math>. 
This can be solved numerically or analytically. Like in the [[Kerr metric|Kerr]] and [[Kerr–Newman metric|Kerr–Newman]] metrics, the horizons have constant Boyer–Lindquist <math>\rm r</math>, while the ergospheres' radii also depend on the polar angle <math>\theta</math>.

This gives 3 positive solutions each (including the black hole's inner and outer horizons and ergospheres as well as the cosmic ones) and a negative solution for the space at <math>\rm r<0</math> in the [[Multiverse#Twin-world_models| antiverse]]<ref>Andrew Hamilton: [http://jila.colorado.edu/~ajsh/insidebh/penrose.html#kerr Black hole Penrose diagrams] (JILA Colorado)</ref><ref>[https://www.researchgate.net/figure/The-Penrose-Carter-diagram-of-the-maximal-Kerr-de-Sitter-spacetime-along-the-symmetry_fig2_338904795 Figure 2] in {{cite journal|last1=Stuchlik|last2=Kološ|last3=Kovář
 |last4=Slany|title=Influence of Cosmic Repulsion and Magnetic Fields on Accretion Disks Rotating around Kerr Black Holes|journal=Universe|date=2020 |volume=6 |issue=2 |page=26 |doi=10.3390/universe6020026|bibcode=2020Univ....6...26S |issn=2218-1997 |doi-access=free }}</ref> behind the [[ring singularity]], which is part of the probably unphysical extended solution of the metric.

With a negative <math>\Lambda</math> (the [[Anti-de_Sitter_space|anti–de–Sitter]] variant with an attractive cosmological constant), there are no cosmic horizon and ergosphere, only the black hole-related ones. 

In the Nariai limit<ref>Leonard Susskind: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=asJYkCQ8uJU&t=2307s Aspects of de Sitter Holography], timestamp 38:27: video of the online seminar on de Sitter space and Holography, Sept 14, 2021</ref> the black hole's outer horizon and ergosphere coincide with the cosmic ones (in the [[De Sitter–Schwarzschild metric|Schwarzschild–de–Sitter metric]] to which the KNdS reduces with <math>\rm a= \mho =0</math> that would be the case when <math>\Lambda=1/9</math>).

== Invariants ==

The [[Ricci_curvature|Ricci scalar]] for the KNdS metric is <math>\rm R=-4 \Lambda</math>, and the [[Kretschmann scalar]] is

<math>\rm K=\{220 a^{12} \Lambda ^2 \cos (6 \theta )+66 a^{12} \Lambda ^2 \cos (8 \theta )+12 a^{12} \Lambda ^2 \cos (10 \theta )+a^{12} \Lambda ^2 \cos (12 \theta )+</math>

<math>\rm 462 a^{12} \Lambda ^2+1080 a^{10} \Lambda ^2 r^2 \cos (6 \theta )+240 a^{10} \Lambda ^2 r^2 \cos (8 \theta )+24 a^{10} \Lambda ^2 r^2 \cos (10 \theta )+</math>

<math>\rm 3024 a^{10} \Lambda ^2 r^2+1920 a^8 \Lambda ^2 r^4 \cos (6 \theta )+ 240 a^8 \Lambda ^2 r^4 \cos (8 \theta )+8400 a^8 \Lambda ^2 r^4-</math>

<math>\rm 1152 a^6 \cos (6 \theta )-11520 a^6 +1280 a^6 \Lambda ^2 r^6 \cos (6 \theta )+12800 a^6 \Lambda ^2 r^6+207360 a^4  r^2-</math>

<math>\rm 138240 a^4  r \mho ^2+11520 a^4 \Lambda ^2 r^8+16128 a^4 \mho ^4-276480 a^2 r^4+368640 a^2 r^3 \mho ^2+</math>

<math>\rm 6144 a^2 \Lambda ^2 r^{10}-104448 a^2 r^2 \mho ^4+3 a^4 \cos (4 \theta ) [ 165 a^8 \Lambda ^2+960 a^6 \Lambda ^2 r^2+2240 a^4 \Lambda ^2 r^4-</math>

<math>\rm 256 a^2 (9-10 \Lambda ^2 r^6)+256 (90 r^2-60 r \mho ^2+5 \Lambda ^2 r^8+7 \mho ^4) ] +24 a^2 \cos (2 \theta ) [ 33 a^{10} \Lambda ^2+</math>

<math>\rm 210 a^8 \Lambda ^2 r^2+560 a^6 \Lambda ^2 r^4-80 a^4 (9-10 \Lambda ^2 r^6)+128 a^2 (90 r^2-60 r \mho ^2+5 \Lambda ^2 r^8+</math>

<math>\rm 7 \mho ^4)+256 r^2 (-45 r^2+60 r \mho ^2+\Lambda ^2 r^8-17 \mho ^4) ] +36864 r^6-73728 r^5 \mho ^2+</math>

<math>\rm 2048 \Lambda ^2 r^{12}+43008 r^4 \mho ^4 \} \div \{12 [ a^2 \cos (2 \theta )+a^2+2 r^2 ] ^6 \}\text{.}</math>
